system.description:
Self-assertive, confident and energetic. Some call you brash; you act rather than wait to learn more.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Energetic: +2 to your Speed Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{Initiative}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Intellect defense or endurance.

  • Suggested Inability: You were never good at studying or retaining facts. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.1ed6a9dae4acd3cb]{Researching}.
Your reactions are honed, easing your initiative tasks in combat.

Bravery is a conscious choice for you, not an absence of fear, and you can instil it in others.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Resolve: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Stealth or Might defense.

  • Suggested Inability: You're brave, but you have to talk yourself into it. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{Initiative}.
You're adept at winning people to your side of an argument through truthful reasoning, understanding, and kindness.

Helping others is your calling, whether by treating injuries or keeping morale up.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Helpful: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.Y191mjA7nOu48LWp]{Healing}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Persuasion or psychology.

  • Suggested Inability: You're too much of a people person to dissemble well. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.9NS4fm5VOrlzRwHv]{Deception}.
You can attempt to diagnose physical illness, and you are skilled with healing tasks.

You study the particulars before you charge in. Others call it timid; you call it sense.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Cognizant: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.S9WFjHa5QI83AFQO]{Perception}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Researching or initiative.

  • Suggested Inability: Sometimes your caution leads to doubt. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.
You have a better chance to notice what others miss when searching an area, listening closely, or using some other sense to discover what is hidden or not obvious.

Jovial and outgoing. You meet each new challenge with a grin and put others at ease.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Witty: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Performance or healing.

  • Suggested Inability: You're lighthearted but not fast. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense}.
You're adept at winning people to your side of an argument through truthful reasoning, understanding, and kindness.

You question claims others take for granted, and you have often been right to.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Skeptical: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Any scientific area of knowledge, such as physics or astronomy.

  • Suggested Inability: You're so absorbed in working out what's going on that you're slow to react. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense}.
You're practiced at ascertaining another character's lies, motives, and disposition.

The figure lurking quietly in the corner. Nobody knows where you came from or what you want.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{Stealth}.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Deception or occultism.

  • Suggested Inability: You have almost as much trouble reading others as they do you. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.
You're adept at sneaking and hiding, staying out of sight, and keeping any noise of your presence to a minimum.
You are practiced at holding your nerve against fear, deceit, and anything that reaches for your mind.

A stickler for accuracy and detail. Everything you own is catalogued and in its place.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Careful: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.uzlopmNCJj8CpFlC]{Forensics}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Researching or identifying.

  • Suggested Inability: You can't stand disruptions, especially to your concentration. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.
You know how to interpret physical evidence to work out what happened at a location, such as a crime scene, or what led to an object's current condition, such as a cause of death.

Fight, flight or freeze — you have only ever felt the urge to fight. A true thrill-seeker.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Dauntless: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Endurance or initiative.

  • Suggested Inability: Your fearlessness makes you impatient. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{Stealth}.
You are practiced at holding your nerve against fear, deceit, and anything that reaches for your mind.

Something in you screams to make them pay. You fold it away for your friends, but it is always there.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Brutish: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.SbEfC3bQGCbTDvOM]{Tracking}.

  • Bloodthirsty: Once you begin fighting, you see only red. The first attack you make in any given combat is eased.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Bloodthirsty characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You're easily provoked. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.
You know how to track a target through natural landscapes and urban environments.

You treat setbacks as stepping stones, and your empathy shows you others' inner battles.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Resilient: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Persuasion or performance.

  • Suggested Inability: You always hope for the best, even when you should be preparing. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.1ed6a9dae4acd3cb]{Researching}.
You're practiced at ascertaining another character's lies, motives, and disposition.

You hunt the mysteries and occult secrets of the world, usually through somebody's archive.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Curious: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.1ed6a9dae4acd3cb]{Researching}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Any knowledge skill, such as astronomy, geography, or history.

  • Suggested Inability: When you see something interesting, you hesitate as you take it all in. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{Initiative}.
You're skilled at gathering information from databases and physical archives, or by hitting the pavement and asking around. Every form of research takes at least a few hours.

Imposing in manner, stature, or both. There is a touch of danger about you, and people sense it.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Threatening: +2 to your Might Pool, or +2 to your Intellect Pool, or +1 to both Pools.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.TxjNz86eOB6UwTGb]{Intimidation}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Gunsmithing or deception.

  • Suggested Inability: You're threatening but not a quick study. Tasks related to lore and knowledge are hindered.
You're good at swaying others with threatening words and/or fearsome presence.

Charming and charismatic. People like you, want to help you, and want to be your friend.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Charismatic: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.

  • Contact: You have an important contact in an influential position, such as a minor celebrity, a police captain, or the editor of a news organisation. Work out the details with the GM.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Contact characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: Your willpower is not one of your strong points. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.
You're adept at winning people to your side of an argument through truthful reasoning, understanding, and kindness.

You are strong, and you enjoy the power and endurance that comes with it.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Strong: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.4057b66c1d139a6d]{Endurance}.

  • Breaking: Your tasks to smash physical objects — doors, containers, and other inanimate objects — are eased.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Breaking characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You're strong but not quick. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{Initiative}.
Regular training has improved your physical fitness, easing your climbing, jumping, and swimming tasks, plus similar feats that require sustained strength.

The world is full of unsettling things and you are not imagining it. The unease keeps you on your toes.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Jumpy: +2 to your Speed Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{Initiative}.

  • High-Strung: You gain an asset to your initiative tasks if you use your first action in an encounter to move a short distance away from whatever threatens you.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the High-Strung characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You'll never convincingly make ultimatums. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.TxjNz86eOB6UwTGb]{Intimidation}.
Your reactions are honed, easing your initiative tasks in combat.

You hate frills, chitchat and gossip. You prize straight talk and the facts.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Austere: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.1ed6a9dae4acd3cb]{Researching}.

  • Resilient: You ignore the first 3 points of Stress you would otherwise take in a day from shock, such as Stress from experiencing something supernatural. Once that threshold is passed you suffer Stress normally until after your next ten-hour recovery roll, which resets it.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Resilient characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: People react badly to your humourless ways. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.
You're skilled at gathering information from databases and physical archives, or by hitting the pavement and asking around. Every form of research takes at least a few hours.

Some formative loss or judgement drives you, and no setback stops you pursuing it.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Dogged: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.Pcfq6GwGkU5Qi90s]{Identifying}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Any craft-related skill, such as carpentry, cooking, leatherworking, metalworking, or sewing.

  • Suggested Inability: You come across as so single-minded that you put people off. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.
Your analytical mind lets you venture a guess regarding the origin of unfamiliar objects, texts, sounds, and so on.

You are sure you know the best way to handle anything, and few can change your mind.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Willful: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Any technical expertise skill, such as programming, publishing, or researching.

  • Suggested Inability: Pomposity doesn't lend itself to likeability. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.
You are practiced at holding your nerve against fear, deceit, and anything that reaches for your mind.

Right place, right time — or more often, out of the wrong place in time. Not luck: speed.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Swift: Quick offers no initial skill, but a larger stat Pool bonus.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Endurance or gymnastics.

  • Suggested Inability: You're quick, but not quick-witted when it comes to falsehoods. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.9NS4fm5VOrlzRwHv]{Deception}.

You harden your heart to others' suffering. What they call cruelty, you call pragmatism.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Hard: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.9NS4fm5VOrlzRwHv]{Deception}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Intimidation or stealth.

  • Suggested Inability: You have a hard time connecting with others or sharing their feelings. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.
You are a capable liar, able to use speech and the written word to deceive and misinform others.

You studied, alone or with an instructor, and you are an expert in a couple of fields.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Studied: Scholarly offers no initial stat Pool bonus, but another skill instead.

  • Skill: You're trained in One knowledge skill, such as philosophy, geography, or history.

  • Skill: You're trained in Another, different knowledge skill, such as astronomy, biology, or geology.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Identifying or researching.

  • Suggested Inability: You spend too long on scholarly pursuits to trust your empathy. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.
You are well-versed in the study of the stars, planets, and cosmology in general.
You have a deep working knowledge of living systems, including animals, plants, and insects.

A sharp memory and a quick grasp of ideas, formal education or not.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Brainy: Smart offers no initial skill, but a larger stat Pool bonus.

  • Eidetic: You remember and can memorise things you experience directly. If a roll is needed to test your memory against something particularly challenging, that roll is eased.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Eidetic characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You're good at absorbing information, but not at hiding what you know. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.9NS4fm5VOrlzRwHv]{Deception}.

Tough enough to take a lot of punishment. You feel the pain; you just don't let it stop you.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Rugged: Sturdy offers no initial skill, but a larger stat Pool bonus.

  • Resilient: You ignore the first 3 points of Stress you would otherwise take in a day from physical sources, such as Stress from minor wounds. Once that threshold is passed you suffer Stress normally until after your next ten-hour recovery roll, which resets it.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Resilient characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You're brawny but not mentally flexible. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}.

You see the patterns others overlook, and you are sure the deepest truths will come into focus.

You gain the following characteristics:

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.8d7248fff87386d3]{Occultism}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Instead of an extra skill, you may take the Throw Salt characteristic.

  • Suggested Inability: You're willing to believe a lot. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.

  • Guarded: +2 to your Might Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{Discerning motive}.

  • Suggested Second Skill: Initiative or perception.

  • Suggested Inability: Sometimes you're too suspicious and put people off. You have an inability in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.c4b6b98d92624257]{Persuasion}.

Devices have always fascinated you. Give you a new one and you'll use it like a pro, or open it up.

  • Technical: +2 to your Intellect Pool.

  • Skill: You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.dbd4639749e26c4b]{Programming} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.20c7b98c5ef86c52]{Electronics}

Starting Pools: Might 10, Speed 9, Intellect 9, plus 6 points to assign as you wish.

Lies, mockery or vile language against a foe who understands you. If successful, it's stunned and can't act for one round, then dazed the next round with its tasks hindered. Action.

Insidious, terrifying words deal 3 points of Stress (4 points of damage to NPCs) to up to five people you choose within short range who can hear and understand you. Make a separate attack roll against each. Action.

Pick one defense task type you're trained in (Might, Speed or Intellect) and become specialized in it. You can take this up to three times, once per defense type. Enabler.

Cost: 6 Intellect points.

A creature you speak with for at least ten minutes loses all its accumulated Stress. Action to initiate.

You form an uncanny, permanent bond with one person or creature: you understand each other without a shared language, even through a single sense (seeing but not hearing, or the reverse). One bond at a time. Action.

Learn one random fact about a creature, object or place relevant to a topic you name. Alternatively, learn a creature's level, but then you can't learn anything else about it with this ability. Action.

Supernatural ability: available only once you have gained 10 levels of Stress from supernatural sources (p27), or from first tier with the Occultist's Already Tainted.

Send a message of up to ten words, or an image, into the mind of someone you know well within 1 mile (1.6 km). Each extra Intellect point adds another mile. Action.

You're dangerous with a firearm in hand. Long practice keeps you steady under fire. You might be a cop, a criminal, a hunter or someone who decided to protect themselves, and you dress so the gun is hidden, close at hand, or both.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. You once winged another PC during target practice and badly hurt them. They decide whether they resent, fear or forgive you.

  2. You overheard another PC say nobody should own a gun. You can prove them right or wrong.

  3. Another PC's mother gave you the gun you carry.

  4. Another PC thinks you're famous for something you never did. You decide whether to correct them.

Additional Equipment: A firearm and three magazines of ammunition.

GM Intrusions: The gun misfires or jams: the attack fails, the action is lost, and another action is needed to clear it.

system.description:
You've drifted through plenty of jobs and nothing has stuck. You take life easy, pick things up, and move on when they get dull, so you know a little about a lot. You dress casually and might be fit or bookish, whichever suits you.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC has always been there for you and has bailed you out more than once.

  2. Another PC is far too uptight. You hope to be the one who teaches them to relax.

  3. You're a bit jealous of another PC, who beats you at your favourite hobby.

  4. You owe another PC money and fully mean to pay it back once things go your way.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Something you've lived through eases your next action.

Major Effect Suggestion: You get a free recovery roll that takes no action.

GM Intrusions: New situations confuse and stress you. Past actions, or failures to act, come back to haunt you.

Cellars, empty houses, tunnels and caves feel like home to you, and open skies may make you uneasy. The dark is where lost things turn up. You wear dark clothes to blend in, or sensible gear for serious work below ground.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC has been your partner on past expeditions. When you both work on the same noncombat task, you each gain an asset.

  2. You think you once saw two other PCs doing something illegal through a keyhole. You choose whether to share it; they choose whether it was really them.

  3. One other PC always seems to hear you, however quietly you move.

  4. One other PC is so loud that you feel bound to teach them to move quietly, whether they want lessons or not.

Minor Effect Suggestion: The target is dazed for a round, and all its tasks are hindered.

Major Effect Suggestion: The target is stunned and loses its next turn.

GM Intrusions: Belongings slip out of pockets in the dark and maps go missing. Information you gather leaves out something important.

abilitySnapshot.description: You ignore penalties for any action, including fighting, in very dim light or cramped spaces. With Eyes Adjusted, that holds even in total darkness. You're trained in stealth tasks while in dim light or none.

abilitySnapshot.description: Using a light source, you make a melee attack. It deals no damage, but if it hits, the target is blinded for one minute.

abilitySnapshot.name: Dark Flow
abilitySnapshot.description: For one hour you're immersed in working in the dark. When you apply a level of Effort to stealth, lockpicking, endurance or perception tasks in dim light or darkness, you get two free levels of Effort on that task. Action to initiate.

system.description:
The only thing that matters in a fight is who wins. You bite, trip, throw dirt, taunt and lie, and you keep a few nasty surprises hidden on you: a blade in a boot, a razor in a hem, powder in a secret pocket.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC is good in a fight, and a few of your tricks would make them great.

  2. Another PC taught you some of your tricks.

  3. Another PC doesn't seem to approve of your methods.

  4. You beat another PC in a fight long ago, using your tactics. They want a friendly rematch and say they're ready for you.

Additional Equipment: An easily hidden weapon and one dose of level 3 poison that inflicts 6 points of damage.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Your foe trips and falls prone.

Major Effect Suggestion: You tangle the foe's legs. They fall and lose their next turn.

GM Intrusions: People think poorly of cheats. Sometimes a dirty trick backfires.

abilitySnapshot.name: Taking Advantage
abilitySnapshot.description: When a foe is prone, weakened, dazed, stunned, moved down the damage track or otherwise at a disadvantage, your attacks against it are eased, on top of any other modifiers from that disadvantage.

abilitySnapshot.name: Eye Gouge
abilitySnapshot.description: You attack a creature that has an eye. The attack is hindered, but on a hit the creature struggles to see for the next hour, and its tasks that rely on sight (most of them) are hindered.

abilitySnapshot.name: Spot Weakness
abilitySnapshot.description: If a creature you can see has a special weakness, such as a vulnerability to fire or a poor perception, you know it. Ask and the GM tells you.

abilitySnapshot.name: Surprise Attack
abilitySnapshot.description: When you attack from hiding, with surprise, or before your opponent has acted, you gain an asset on the attack and deal 2 extra points of damage on a hit.

abilitySnapshot.name: Mind Games
abilitySnapshot.description: You hit a foe that understands you with lies, mockery or vile language. On a success it is stunned and can't act for one round, then dazed the following round, with its tasks hindered.

abilitySnapshot.name: Capable Fighter
abilitySnapshot.description: Your attacks deal 1 extra point of damage.

abilitySnapshot.name: Using the Environment
abilitySnapshot.description: You turn your surroundings to your advantage. For ten minutes, your attack rolls and Speed defense rolls are eased. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Twisting the Knife
abilitySnapshot.description: In a round after you hit a foe with a melee weapon, you can automatically deal that weapon's standard damage to it again, with no modifiers: 2 points for a light weapon, 4 for medium, 6 for heavy.

abilitySnapshot.name: Murderer
abilitySnapshot.description: A sudden strike to a vital spot kills a target of level 4 or lower outright. Each extra level of Effort raises the maximum target level by 1.

system.description:
Helping your friends with small things and big ones is simply who you are. Maybe you always had friends, maybe you never did until now, or maybe you lost them and want another chance. When a friend needs a hand, you offer it without thinking.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. The first time you saw a friend in trouble, you didn't help. You suspect another PC (that friend) doesn't know, and you're thinking of telling them.

  2. You helped another PC with something mildly illegal. You feel guilty, and a little angry at them, though it was your choice.

  3. Another PC has always been there for you when you couldn't help yourself.

  4. You and another PC tried to help a mutual friend and failed. That friend is gone now, and you feel it's your fault. You don't know if they blame you.

Additional Equipment: A photo of you and your friends.

Optional: You can swap one ability from your type for Advice From a Friend. @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.aeba27869b0a6672]{Advice From a Friend}.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Your coaching eases a friend's next action.

Major Effect Suggestion: Your help gives a friend a free recovery roll that takes no action.

GM Intrusions: Others sometimes have hidden motives. The law takes too much interest. Even when everything goes right, there are repercussions.

abilitySnapshot.name: Friendly Help
abilitySnapshot.description: If a friend fails a task and you help, they can retry it without spending Effort for the retry. This works even if you're not trained in the task.

abilitySnapshot.name: Courageous
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in Intellect defense and initiative tasks.

abilitySnapshot.name: Weather the Vicissitudes
abilitySnapshot.description: Ignore the first point of Stress you gain each day. This resets after your ten-hour rest.

abilitySnapshot.name: Buddy System
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick a character next to you to be your buddy for ten minutes. You're trained in all tasks to find, heal, interact with or protect them, and while you stand next to each other you both have an asset on Speed defense tasks. You can have only one buddy at a time. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Attacks
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

abilitySnapshot.name: In Harm's Way
abilitySnapshot.description: When you spend your action putting your friends first, defense tasks are eased for any adjacent characters you choose until the end of your next turn. During that time, if one of those friends gains Stress you can take up to half of it (rounded up) instead, and if one would suffer a serious injury you can take it instead, as long as you're not already impaired or debilitated.

abilitySnapshot.name: Enhanced Physique
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 3 points to split between your Might and Speed Pools however you like.

abilitySnapshot.name: Inspire Action
abilitySnapshot.description: Tell one ally who can see and understand you to take an action. If they take exactly that action, they do it immediately as an extra action, and it doesn't use up their normal action on their turn.

abilitySnapshot.name: Deep Consideration
abilitySnapshot.description: When you plan with your friends to reach a goal together, ask the GM one very general question about how the plan is likely to go and get a short answer. Each of you also gains an asset on one roll that carries out the plan, if you act on it within a few days.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Defense
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one defense task you aren't trained in: Might defense, Speed defense or Intellect defense. You become trained in it.

system.description:
Subtlety, guile and stealth are your trade, honed over years of practice. You use disguises and tools, but your training matters most. Infiltrators are often spies, agents or undercover officers, and sometimes thieves or assassins.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. You watched another PC from a distance for a while before you met and became allies. You decide whether to tell them.

  2. However hard you try, you can't hide from one other PC.

  3. You and two other PCs once worked a mission together, then fell out.

  4. Another PC is your sibling (if their player agrees), and you look very alike.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Your moves startle the opponent so much that they're dazed and their tasks are hindered.

Major Effect Suggestion: Every opponent within short range is startled and dazed, with their tasks hindered.

GM Intrusions: Spies are punished harshly when caught, and allies disown infiltrators who get caught. Some secrets are better left buried.

abilitySnapshot.name: Stealthy
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in two of these skills of your choice: deception, disguise, lockpicking, pickpocketing or stealth. You can take this ability more than once, choosing different skills each time.

abilitySnapshot.name: Sense Attitudes
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in discerning motive.

abilitySnapshot.name: Impersonate
abilitySnapshot.description: For one hour you change your voice, posture and mannerisms and throw together a disguise, gaining an asset to pass as someone else, either a specific person or a general role. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Flight Not Fight
abilitySnapshot.description: If you use your action only to move, your Speed defense tasks are eased.

abilitySnapshot.name: Awareness
abilitySnapshot.description: When you spend a level of Effort on a perception task, you get one extra free level of Effort on it.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Attacks
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

abilitySnapshot.name: Nearly Invisible
abilitySnapshot.description: For ten minutes you commit fully to staying unseen. While hiding, you're specialized in stealth and Speed defense tasks. The effect ends if you reveal yourself (attacking, using an ability, moving something large), but you can take an action to hide again and restore it. Action to initiate or reinitiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Evasion
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in all defense tasks.

abilitySnapshot.name: Brainwashing
abilitySnapshot.description: With trickery and smooth lies, you make a target of level 3 or lower do as you say. On a successful Intellect attack, you direct the actions of a target you speak to for one minute, letting them act freely or overriding them case by case, as long as you can see and direct them. If someone challenges what they're doing, you need another successful Intellect attack to reassure them or they stop. Each extra level of Effort can raise the target's maximum level by 1 or add a minute. Action to initiate. The book advises handling this with care and never using it on PCs.

abilitySnapshot.name: Spring Away
abilitySnapshot.description: Whenever you succeed on a Speed defense roll, you can immediately move up to a short distance. Once per round.

system.description:
Through charisma, natural authority and maybe some training, you get others to follow you willingly. You might be a politician, captain or manager. You carry yourself to inspire, charm or intimidate, and your voice carries over any noise.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC used to follow you, but now you see them as an equal.

  2. Another PC recently mocked you in a way that really hurt. How you deal with it is up to you.

  3. Another PC introduces you to the follower you gain at tier 2.

  4. Another PC looks so much like you that you suspect you're half-siblings.

Minor Effect Suggestion: The next time you try to influence the same foe, the task is eased.

Major Effect Suggestion: The foe stays persuaded, deceived, intimidated or otherwise influenced for twice as long.

GM Intrusions: Followers fail, betray you, lie, become corrupted, get kidnapped or die.

  • Tier 2: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.62dc55bc1fb84fca]{Enhanced Potential}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.265d686160cd7a6d]{Basic Follower}

  • Tier 3: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.ec964341892a4aac]{Advanced Command} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.39207905d160ff36]{Expert Follower}.

  • Tier 4: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.8c3de0e98bc29ddd]{Captivate or Inspire}

Followers (p71): Followers don't need pay, food or housing. The PC usually rolls for a follower. A follower's level is how many tasks they have a modification in, chosen when you gain them. When helping you, a follower grants an asset on a task they have a modification for, and acts as if they had an inability in everything else. Acting on their own, a modification raises their effective level by one for that task.

A follower can't grant an asset to attacks or defense until they're level 3, and then only with a matching modification. A follower gains a level (and a new modification) each time you advance two tiers after gaining them. The GM may occasionally offer an exceptional follower, one level higher than normal. A follower can be a pet if it makes sense.

The GM may ask you to actually go and find a suitable follower when you take Basic Follower.

abilitySnapshot.name: Basic Follower

While you keep doing nothing but issue commands, you can give that target a new one each turn. It ends when you stop or they leave short range. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Expert Follower
abilitySnapshot.description: You gain a level 3 follower with no restriction on their modifications. You can take this more than once. Instead of a new level 3 follower, you can raise an existing level 2 follower to level 3 and gain a new level 2 follower.

abilitySnapshot.name: Captivate or Inspire
abilitySnapshot.description: Use your words one of two ways. Either all NPCs of level 2 or lower who hear you stay fixed on you for as long as you keep talking, or all NPCs who hear you act as one level higher for the next hour. You pick which NPCs are affected. Attacking anyone in the crowd breaks their attention. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Potential
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to split among your stat Pools however you like.

abilitySnapshot.name: Band of Followers
abilitySnapshot.description: You gain four level 3 followers with no restriction on their modifications.

abilitySnapshot.name: Mind of a Leader
abilitySnapshot.description: When you plan how to handle a future situation, ask the GM one very general question about how the plan is likely to go and get a short answer.

system.description:
You don't have your dream job, but you get by. Events may have pushed you here, or your break just hasn't come yet. You work hard, handle trouble as it comes and pick things up fast. You dress to blend in, because standing out draws the wrong attention.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC helped you land your current job.

  2. Through no fault of their own, another PC got you fired from your last job.

  3. Another PC is your cousin.

  4. You're fairly sure another PC hates you, though you don't know why.

Additional Equipment: Two tickets to a show at a local cinema.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Your next task, attack or defense roll within one minute is eased.

Major Effect Suggestion: Treat your next task, attack or defense roll within one minute as a natural 18.

GM Intrusions: Accidents and mistakes are great teachers.

system.description:
You're a scrapper who meets problems head-on and physically. You don't hide or back down, and your friends feel safer heading into danger with you beside them. You probably dress loud so you stand out.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Past events made you watch over another PC. They're your default charge for your tier 2 Protector ability.

  2. One or two other PCs seem tough, and you secretly hope to find out who's tougher.

  3. When another PC is within immediate range during a fight, they sometimes ease your attacks and sometimes accidentally hinder them (50% chance each way, rolled per fight).

  4. You used to be in a relationship with another PC. It ended long ago.

Additional Equipment: A melee weapon of your choice.

Minor Effect Suggestion: The target is dazed for a round, with all its tasks hindered.

Major Effect Suggestion: A piece of equipment your opponent wears or holds is destroyed.

GM Intrusions: Weapons break or fly out of your grip. Brawlers trip. Things on the battlefield fall or collapse.

system.description:
You have uncanny balance and coordination. You move with grace, rarely knock anything over, land well when you fall and often avoid danger altogether. You wear close-fitting clothes and carry little.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC's clumsiness and noise annoy you.

  2. Another PC comes from the same place as you, and you knew each other as children.

  3. You help another PC with advice and a steadying hand. When you're next to each other, their @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.DbWx19J2Bkv12OpZ]{gymnastics} tasks are eased.

  4. Another PC owes you a lot of money.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to your Speed Pool.

abilitySnapshot.name: Hard to Hit
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in Speed defense tasks. You gain this alongside whichever tier 3 ability you choose.

abilitySnapshot.name: Quick Strike
abilitySnapshot.description: You make a melee attack so fast it's hard to defend against. The attack is eased by two steps, and a foe you hit takes normal damage and is dazed, with its tasks hindered next round.

abilitySnapshot.name: Slippery
abilitySnapshot.description: Tasks to escape any bond or grasp are eased.

abilitySnapshot.name: Perfect Speed Burst
abilitySnapshot.description: You take two separate actions this round.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to your Speed Pool.

system.description:
You are the weapon. Punches, kicks and full-body moves let you hurt foes badly without draining yourself. You learned through training, the military or a rough upbringing, and you keep your body in top shape. You wear loose clothes and rarely carry anything but maybe knuckle or boot weapons.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC thinks a real weapon is something you hold, and may look down on you.

  2. Another PC is so unaware of their body that they keep getting in your way. If you miss and hit someone nearby by accident, it's likely them.

  3. You once trained with a close friend of another PC, and you owe that friend a great deal.

  4. Two other PCs asked to become your students, but only one shows any talent.

Minor Effect Suggestion: You trip the target and knock it prone.

Major Effect Suggestion: You strike a limb, making it useless for the next minute.

GM Intrusions: Hitting some foes hurts you as much as them. Armed opponents have longer reach. Complicated moves can throw you off balance.

  • Tier 2: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.008069c90d155613]{Advantage to Disadvantage}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.17aa16b31801e8ca]{Unarmed Fighting Style}

abilitySnapshot.name: Fists of Fury
abilitySnapshot.description: Your unarmed attacks deal 2 extra points of damage.

abilitySnapshot.name: Scarred and Hardened
abilitySnapshot.description: Reduce the Stress you suffer from physical injury by 1 (by 2 if your type already gives you this ability). Stress from mental shock or despair is unaffected.

abilitySnapshot.name: Advantage to Disadvantage
abilitySnapshot.description: You attack an armed foe with a flurry of moves, dealing damage and disarming them. Their weapon ends up in your hands or 10 feet (3.5 m) away on the ground, your choice. This attack is hindered.

abilitySnapshot.name: Unarmed Fighting Style
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in unarmed attacks.

abilitySnapshot.name: Moving Like Water
abilitySnapshot.description: You flow and spin so that for one minute all your attacks and Speed defense tasks gain an asset.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Potential
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to split among your stat Pools however you like.

abilitySnapshot.name: Stand Like Iron
abilitySnapshot.description: The next attack this encounter that would give you a serious injury gives you 2 points of Stress instead.

abilitySnapshot.name: Stun Attack
abilitySnapshot.description: As part of a melee or ranged attack, attempt a difficulty 5 Speed task. On a success, your attack deals normal damage and the creature is stunned and loses its next turn. On a failure you still roll the attack normally but can't stun.

abilitySnapshot.name: Master of Unarmed Fighting Style
abilitySnapshot.description: You're specialized in unarmed attacks. If you already are, your unarmed attacks deal 2 extra points of damage instead.

abilitySnapshot.name: Lethal Damage
abilitySnapshot.description: Your unarmed attacks deal 5 extra points of damage when they hit.

system.description:
When others give up, you're only getting started. Resilience and stubborn determination carry you through. You don't fuss over your appearance and you're not much of a talker. You act.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. You feel an overwhelming need to impress another PC, and you're not sure why.

  2. Another PC is capable but needs motivating, and you keep urging them to keep going.

  3. You feel protective of another PC and don't want to see them hurt.

  4. Another PC says they've known you for years, but you barely remember them.

Minor Effect Suggestion: You restore 2 points to your Might Pool.

Major Effect Suggestion: Your next action is eased by two steps.

GM Intrusions: Sometimes it's your equipment or weapons that give out.

abilitySnapshot.name: Improved Recovery
abilitySnapshot.description: Your ten-minute recovery roll takes one action instead, so your first two recovery rolls take one action each, the third one hour and the fourth ten hours.

abilitySnapshot.name: Push on Through
abilitySnapshot.description: For one hour you ignore the effects of terrain while moving.

abilitySnapshot.name: Tough
abilitySnapshot.description: You gain an extra step on your damage track, called hurt, between hale and impaired. Hurt has no other effect; you're sore and bruised but fine.

abilitySnapshot.name: Stand Like Iron
abilitySnapshot.description: The next attack this encounter that would give you a serious injury gives you 2 points of Stress instead.

abilitySnapshot.name: Hidden Reserves
abilitySnapshot.description: When you make a recovery roll, you also gain +1 to your Might Edge and your Speed Edge for the next ten minutes.

abilitySnapshot.name: Outlast the Foe
abilitySnapshot.description: After five full rounds of combat, you have an asset on all tasks for the rest of that combat and deal 1 extra point of damage per attack.

abilitySnapshot.name: Not Dead Yet
abilitySnapshot.description: While debilitated, you can act as if you were only impaired. You're still one step from death.

abilitySnapshot.name: Final Defiance
abilitySnapshot.description: When you would die, you stay conscious and active, debilitated, for one more round, plus another round each time you succeed on a difficulty 5 Might task. If someone else succeeds on a difficulty 5 healing task on you during that time, you survive, still debilitated. If you reach dead again while in this state, you can't be saved.

abilitySnapshot.name: Ignore Affliction
abilitySnapshot.description: Ignore an unwanted condition or affliction (disease, paralysis, mind control, a broken limb and so on, but not Stress or the damage track) and act as if it doesn't affect you for one hour. A condition that would last less than an hour is negated entirely.

system.description:
The internet has been your home since you first opened a browser. Websites, social media, gaming, streaming, forums, apps: you know the latest news, jokes and places that matter. You dress so casually it's sometimes inappropriate, and you may forget mirrors exist.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. You knew another PC online long before you met in person.

  2. Another PC says you spend too much time online and tells you to go outside. Charming or just annoying? You decide.

  3. Another PC believes you've dug up their personal information. You decide whether they're right.

  4. Another PC is hopeless with tech and keeps asking you to fix their computer or explain things.

Additional Equipment: A top-of-the-line laptop and smartphone, beyond what an average character could afford.

Minor Effect Suggestion: Your next attempt at anything involving computers is eased.

Major Effect Suggestion: Thinking about how you'll brag online about this, you immediately restore 1d6 + 1 points to your Intellect Pool.

GM Intrusions: Hackers get hacked. Paying attention to the internet leads to doing or saying exactly the wrong thing in real life.

  • Tier 2: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.d5878b17fa525771]{Hacking}

  • Tier 3: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.0bc79a45de0e0459]{Online Contacts} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.5fe8e4c376c3bb73]{Crowdsourcing}.

abilitySnapshot.name: Online Research
abilitySnapshot.description: All researching tasks are eased when you have internet access.

abilitySnapshot.name: Tech Skill
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in one of these skills of your choice: electronics, engineering, programming or researching.

abilitySnapshot.name: Hacking
abilitySnapshot.description: You can pose as someone else online, which might get you into their information, money or credit cards, or let you tip off the authorities about crimes they (probably didn't) commit. Less harmfully, you can learn about them: address, routine, current location. It takes from a minute to many hours, and the difficulty depends on the person's level and their online security; reading someone's email is harder than tracing their family history, and their bank account harder still.

abilitySnapshot.name: Online Contacts
abilitySnapshot.description: You have three contacts you know only online, each with an area of expertise you choose. With online access you can ask them about their field and get a detailed answer within an hour, and answers to follow-up questions within another hour.

abilitySnapshot.name: Crowdsourcing
abilitySnapshot.description: You post a question online and let others help. If you wait for the answers (up to 24 hours), any information-related task, research included, is eased by two steps. Action to initiate.

abilitySnapshot.name: Deep Dive
abilitySnapshot.description: Through the internet, ask the GM one question and get a general answer. The GM sets the level by how obscure it is: something findable elsewhere is level 1, obscure knowledge of the past is level 7. Knowledge of the future is impossible.

abilitySnapshot.name: Better Hacking
abilitySnapshot.description: With electronic access to a system, you try to take control of it: cameras, alarms, electronic locks, tracking, whole email servers, website back ends, databases and so on. The difficulty depends on its protections, usually 3 to 9, and it may take one action or hours.

abilitySnapshot.name: Read It Somewhere
abilitySnapshot.description: After a round of concentration, you recall obscure facts from the internet that ease the task you attempt next round by three steps.

abilitySnapshot.name: Brain Food
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to your Intellect Pool.

system.description:
Running isn't always your answer, but it's your first instinct, and it has saved you more than once. Caution is an art form to you. Once you've judged a threat from somewhere safe, you'll deal with it. You're no coward; you just choose when to engage. You wear comfortable, neutral clothes you can run and hide in.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. While fleeing a threat, you left another PC to fend for themselves. They barely survived. Their player decides whether they resent or forgive you.

  2. Another PC recently put you in danger, by accident or not. You're fine now, but wary of them.

  3. Another PC seems even more nervous than you about something. You'd like to teach them your measured approach to fear.

  4. Another PC doubts your caution is thoughtful and laughs when you explain it. They may have called you a coward.

Additional Equipment: A pair of running shoes that fit perfectly.

Minor Effect Suggestion: You can attempt a stealth task any time before the end of next round.

Major Effect Suggestion: You take an extra action, used only to move a short distance, attempt a stealth action, or move an immediate distance and attempt a stealth action.

GM Intrusions: Quick movements lead to dropped items, slips on uneven ground or wrong turns.

abilitySnapshot.name: Go Defensive
abilitySnapshot.description: In combat, you can enter a state of heightened alertness whenever you like. While in it you can't use Intellect points, but you gain +1 to your Speed Edge and two assets on Speed defense tasks. It lasts until you choose to end it, you attack a foe, or no combat is going on within range of your senses. After it ends, you can't use it again until you've made a recovery roll.

abilitySnapshot.name: Enhanced Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 3 points to your Speed Pool.

abilitySnapshot.name: Quick to Flee
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in stealth and gymnastics.

abilitySnapshot.name: Incredible Running Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: You can move up to a long distance as part of another action. As an action, you can move up to 200 feet (60 m), or up to 500 feet (150 m) with a successful difficulty 4 Speed-based roll.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to your Speed Pool.

abilitySnapshot.name: Increasing Determination
abilitySnapshot.description: If you fail a noncombat physical task (forcing a door, climbing a cliff) and retry it, you don't need to apply a level of Effort to retry, but the retry is still eased. A second failure gives no special benefit.

abilitySnapshot.name: Quick Wits
abilitySnapshot.description: When a task would normally cost points from your Intellect Pool, you can pay with Speed points instead.

abilitySnapshot.name: Go to Ground
abilitySnapshot.description: You move up to a long distance and try to hide, gaining an asset on the stealth task to vanish from everyone who knew you were there.

abilitySnapshot.name: Burst of Escape
abilitySnapshot.description: You take two separate actions this round, as long as one of them is hiding or moving in a direction that isn't toward a foe.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Defense
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one defense task you aren't trained in: Might defense, Speed defense or Intellect defense. You become trained in it.

system.description:
You're a master of deduction. A sharp eye and quick wit let you piece clues together while others are stumped. You might be a detective, but a professor or scientist fits too. You dress practically with a touch of style, maybe carrying a briefcase of tools.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC is the friend who got you reading detective fiction, which became your obsession.

  2. Another PC doesn't seem to trust or like you, and you feel you must win them over.

  3. Another PC is a great sounding board. After an hour talking with them, you gain an asset on any knowledge-based task you're trained in.

  4. You and another PC were rivals in some past endeavour.

Minor Effect Suggestion: You find an additional clue about the mystery you're working on.

Major Effect Suggestion: When you reveal a solution in front of its subject, they're stunned by your brilliance and can't move or act for a round.

GM Intrusions: Evidence disappears, red herrings confuse, witnesses lie, and early research is wrong.

  • Tier 2: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.b5d8edbc3c2d5b64]{Out of Harm's Way}

  • Tier 3: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.23de1c4ccf683536]{You Studied} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.59b7dca327310ed1]{Skill With Attacks}.

abilitySnapshot.name: Investigate
abilitySnapshot.description: You can pay for levels of Effort on any Intellect-based task from your Might, Speed or Intellect Pool.

abilitySnapshot.name: Sleuth
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in perception.

abilitySnapshot.name: Out of Harm's Way
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in Speed defense tasks.

abilitySnapshot.name: You Studied
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in two areas of knowledge of your choice (not physical or combat skills), or specialized in one.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Attacks
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

abilitySnapshot.name: Draw Conclusion
abilitySnapshot.description: After a few minutes of careful observation and investigation (questioning NPCs, searching a room or file), a difficulty 3 Intellect task teaches you a pertinent fact. Each further use is hindered by an extra step, until you rest for ten hours and the difficulty resets to 3.

abilitySnapshot.name: Defuse Situation
abilitySnapshot.description: When questioning provokes anger or violence, you deflect with distraction or evasion. On a successful Intellect attack, a living foe can't attack anyone or anything for one round.

abilitySnapshot.name: Seize the Initiative
abilitySnapshot.description: Within one minute of successfully using Draw Conclusion, you can take one extra, immediate action, even out of turn. You can't use this again until you've rested for ten hours.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Skill With Defense
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one defense task (Might, Speed or Intellect), even one you're trained in. You become trained in it, or specialized if you were already trained. You can take this up to three times, picking a different defense each time.

system.description:
You're a police officer. It's a hard and often thankless job, made worse when bad apples abuse their power, but you take enforcing the law and keeping the peace seriously. Hard questions and your commanding presence often get confessions. On duty you're in uniform with your badge or warrant card on show; off duty you still carry them.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC once trained under you as a cadet (if they agree they were in law enforcement), but has since moved on.

  2. You know another PC spent several months in prison, but not why.

  3. Another PC is an old friend who hates that you're a cop and keeps trying to get you to quit.

  4. There's a warrant on record for another PC, probably unpaid parking fines. You've chosen not to raise it, for now.

Additional Equipment: Police uniform and duty belt (handcuffs, radio, holster, torch), a badge, a gun (medium ranged weapon you're licensed to carry) and a baton (light melee weapon).

Minor Effect Suggestion: The next time you command the same foe, the task is eased.

Major Effect Suggestion: The foe surrenders, or your ability affects them for twice as long.

GM Intrusions: Bystanders react badly when you reveal your authority. A more urgent situation demands your attention.

Abilities by tier:

  • Tier 1: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.43a9c23160cc519d]{Authority}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.51dd19ab2e359b3a]{Driver}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.c73e543e4d3800d1]{Armed Response}

  • Tier 2: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.731998d2f651843f]{Command}

  • Tier 3: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.2a82e9a2546507fe]{Cool Under Fire} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.71d39d3b2f8e97b4]{Insider}.

  • Tier 4: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.0932f9b16bf17947]{Rapid Attack}

  • Tier 5: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.f1da9727bccfe419]{Encouraging Presence}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.40d86c27707e362c]{Skill With Defense}

  • Tier 6: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.feab8d677b18b295]{Greater Enhanced Might or Speed} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.8089438094ff5cf0]{Close to the Chief}.

Badge or warrant card: a real one requires ongoing employment with a police force, though leave, sabbaticals and holidays don't put it at risk. If it's taken away and you use a fake, someone may spot the fraud, though most NPCs won't.

Taking Close to the Chief makes you part of the problem: special treatment is likely a sign of corruption.

abilitySnapshot.name: Authority
abilitySnapshot.description: Your air of authority is an asset on all social interactions. Some people react the opposite way, such as criminals or those the police have wronged, and your interactions with them are hindered instead.

abilitySnapshot.name: Driver
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in driving.

abilitySnapshot.name: Armed Response
abilitySnapshot.description: You're practiced with guns and take no penalty when you use one.

abilitySnapshot.name: Command
abilitySnapshot.description: Using your authority as an officer, you give one simple command to a target within short range who can understand you. On a successful Intellect attack, they try to carry it out as their next action. The command can't directly harm them or their allies ("Flee" might work, "Stab yourself" won't) and must be a single action. They can still defend themselves and strike back if attacked.

abilitySnapshot.name: Cool Under Fire
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in Speed defense tasks.

abilitySnapshot.name: Insider
abilitySnapshot.description: You can get information only law enforcement has: past cases and crimes, identities from licence plates, missing persons details and so on.

abilitySnapshot.name: Rapid Attack
abilitySnapshot.description: Once per round, you can make an extra attack with your gun.

abilitySnapshot.name: Encouraging Presence
abilitySnapshot.description: For one minute, allies within short range gain an asset on defense rolls.

abilitySnapshot.name: Skill With Defense
abilitySnapshot.description: Pick one defense task you aren't trained in: Might defense, Speed defense or Intellect defense. You become trained in it.

abilitySnapshot.name: Greater Enhanced Might or Speed
abilitySnapshot.description: Gain 6 points to your Might Pool, 6 to your Speed Pool, or split 6 points between them.

abilitySnapshot.name: Close to the Chief
abilitySnapshot.description: The chief of police (or equivalent) respects and likes you. Beyond sharing information, they give you room to bend or break the rules. Through them you can see almost any case file, in your department or other agencies (national police, Interpol and the like), and call in backup or help, kept confidential if needed.

system.description:
Thief, burglar, pickpocket: you've made a living in the back alleys at the expense of the rich and careless, whether out of danger or desperation. Those talents serve you well in plenty of other work too. You dress to blend in, and in black when you're on a job.

Connection: Choose one of the following with your group.

  1. Another PC knew you before and helped you leave crime behind, at least for now.

  2. You once tried to steal from another PC, and they caught you.

  3. You can never hide from one particular PC.

  4. Another PC knows your real identity or that you work undercover (if either is secret), and has kept quiet so far.

Additional Equipment: A bag of light tools, including lockpicks.

Minor Effect Suggestion: You can immediately try to hide after this action.

Major Effect Suggestion: You can immediately take a second action this turn.

GM Intrusions: Thieves end up in jail. Powerful enemies are made.

  • Tier 6: Choose @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.194258389f79cf80]{Alley Rat} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.85b0c4e437be54c4]{All-Out Con}.

Underworld contacts are lasting additions to the campaign, limited to what those people know and can do. I Know a Guy is deliberately more open-ended, but its help is temporary.

abilitySnapshot.name: Stealthy
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in two of these skills of your choice: deception, discerning motive, disguise, lockpicking, pickpocketing or stealth. You can take this ability more than once, choosing different skills each time.

abilitySnapshot.name: Underworld Contacts
abilitySnapshot.description: You know many people involved in illegal activity. They aren't necessarily friends or trustworthy, but they see you as one of their own and may owe you a favour. Work out three or four of these contacts with the GM.

abilitySnapshot.name: Pull a Fast One
abilitySnapshot.description: When you run a con, pick a pocket, trick a mark, sneak something past a guard and the like, you gain an asset on the task.

abilitySnapshot.name: I Know a Guy
abilitySnapshot.description: Facing a difficult problem that isn't urgent, you reach someone you know, or know of, who might solve it. They're nearly always on the edges of society: criminals, ex-convicts and the like. Typical help includes fencing or buying illegal goods, forgeries and fake IDs, breaking into computers or phones, getting confidential information, or hiring criminals from burglars to hitmen. Finding them, meeting and agreeing terms usually takes three to seven days, and they expect payment or a favour.

abilitySnapshot.name: Master Thief
abilitySnapshot.description: You're trained in gymnastics and lockpicking.

abilitySnapshot.name: Dirty Fighter
abilitySnapshot.description: You distract, blind, annoy or otherwise hamper a foe, hindering their attacks and defenses for one minute.

abilitySnapshot.name: Alley Rat
abilitySnapshot.description: In a city, you find or make a major shortcut, secret way in or emergency escape route where none seemed to exist. It takes a successful Intellect action at a difficulty the GM sets. Work out the details with the GM.

abilitySnapshot.name: All-Out Con

system.description:

documents.name: Serves as an Avatar: The Buried

system.description:
The Entities sometimes give a person a share of their power, spreading fear in the world. That person is an Avatar. Each Entity makes its own Avatars, directly or not, and may have several or none. The Avatar chooses to accept the gift, even without grasping what it means. Some serve their Entity like a god; unwilling ones hold great power knowing each use feeds something malevolent.

"Serves as an Avatar" is an extra focus added on top of the character's normal focus. This one is for an Avatar of The Buried.

Requirements:

  • Tier 4 or higher.

  • Has gained 10 levels of Stress from paranormal experiences over time.

  • Has at least one supernatural ability from their type.

  • Has died and been reborn, physically or metaphorically: something drastic has changed them in body or mind. A character who seems to die in play and meets the other requirements may return changed, likely only once.

Feeding: An Avatar must feed their Entity or be fed upon. If you don't use your Entity power at least once a week, you gain 3 points of Stress, and 3 more each following day you go without using it.

All Avatars gain: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.7874e3210961b887]{Sense Avatar} and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.focus-abilities.Item.2155ece099f298bc]{Sense Supernatural Activity}.

The Entity powers are suggestions. Work with the GM to customise your Entity-specific power to fit your idea of the Avatar.

documents.name: Does a Bit of This and That

system.description:
Your attacks with guns deal 1 extra point of damage.

Enabler.

You're practiced with guns and take no penalty when you use one.

Enabler.

You can pay for levels of Effort to increase gun damage from either your Speed Pool or your Intellect Pool. Each level adds 3 points of damage to a successful attack, or 5 points if you spent a turn lining up the shot.

Enabler.

Choose one: you become trained with guns, or you gain the Spray ability (cost 2 Speed points).

Enabler.

Your gun attacks deal 3 extra points of damage.

Enabler.

You can make two gun attacks as one action. The second attack is hindered by two steps.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Speed points.

With a rapid-fire weapon, you shoot at up to three targets standing next to one another. Make a separate attack roll for each; every attack is hindered.

Action.

When you hit with a gun, you can deal 1 less point of damage to strike a precise spot. For example, you can knock an object out of a hand, hit a limb the target moves with so its top speed drops to immediate for a few days (or until it gets expert medical care), or sever a strap so a pack or worn device falls off.

Enabler.

Your standard gun attacks deal 5 extra points of damage when they hit.

Enabler.

Pick any two noncombat skills. You become trained in both.

Enabler.

Your ten-minute recovery roll takes only one round.

Enabler.

Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

Enabler.

Cost: 2 Intellect points.

When you attempt a task you're not trained in, you can improvise (a makeshift tool, a flash of insight, plain dumb luck) to gain an asset on it.

Enabler.

Pick one defense task (Might, Speed or Intellect), even one you're trained in. You become trained in it, or specialized if you were already trained. You can take this up to three times, picking a different defense each time.

Enabler.

Gain 6 points to split among your stat Pools however you like.

Enabler.

Cost: 6 Intellect points.

Ask the GM one question and get a general answer. The GM sets the task level by how obscure the answer is: something you could look up elsewhere is level 1, obscure knowledge of the past is level 7. The player is encouraged to describe the past experience that supplies the answer.

Action.

When a task would normally cost points from your Intellect Pool, you can pay with Speed points instead.

Enabler.

You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.S9WFjHa5QI83AFQO]{perception}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.4057b66c1d139a6d]{endurance} and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.DbWx19J2Bkv12OpZ]{gymnastics} tasks.

Enabler.

You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.F1YvwItD8HbRP58l]{lockpicking} and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ySH2x77NNfEDxQ9C]{mechanics}.

Enabler.

Darkness doesn't hinder you, and you can see faintly even in total darkness.

Enabler.

Attacks you make in dim light or darkness get a free level of Effort.

Enabler.

When you apply Effort to escape bonds, squeeze through tight spaces or perform other contortions, you get a free level of Effort. You're also trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} tasks.

Enabler.

Exposure to terrible things has toughened you. Reduce any Stress you gain, from any source, by 1 point.

Enabler.

You ignore penalties for any action, including fighting, in very dim light or cramped spaces. With Eyes Adjusted, that holds even in total darkness. You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{stealth} tasks while in dim light or none.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Speed points.

Using a light source, you make a melee attack. It deals no damage, but if it hits, the target is blinded for one minute.

Action.

Cost: 6 Intellect points.

For one hour you're immersed in working in the dark. When you apply a level of Effort to @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{stealth}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.F1YvwItD8HbRP58l]{lockpicking}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.4057b66c1d139a6d]{endurance} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.S9WFjHa5QI83AFQO]{perception} tasks in dim light or darkness, you get two free levels of Effort on that task. Action to initiate.

Action.

When a foe is prone, weakened, dazed, stunned, moved down the damage track or otherwise at a disadvantage, your attacks against it are eased, on top of any other modifiers from that disadvantage.

Enabler.

Cost: 2 Might points.

You attack a creature that has an eye. The attack is hindered, but on a hit the creature struggles to see for the next hour, and its tasks that rely on sight (most of them) are hindered.

Action.

If a creature you can see has a special weakness, such as a vulnerability to fire or a poor perception, you know it. Ask and the GM tells you.

Enabler.

When you attack from hiding, with surprise, or before your opponent has acted, you gain an asset on the attack and deal 2 extra points of damage on a hit.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Intellect points.

You hit a foe that understands you with lies, mockery or vile language. On a success it is stunned and can't act for one round, then dazed the following round, with its tasks hindered.

Action.

Your attacks deal 1 extra point of damage.

Enabler.

Cost: 4 Intellect points.

You turn your surroundings to your advantage. For ten minutes, your attack rolls and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} rolls are eased. Action to initiate.

Action.

Cost: 4 Might points.

In a round after you hit a foe with a melee weapon, you can automatically deal that weapon's standard damage to it again, with no modifiers: 2 points for a light weapon, 4 for medium, 6 for heavy.

Action.

Cost: 8+ Might points.

A sudden strike to a vital spot kills a target of level 4 or lower outright. Each extra level of Effort raises the maximum target level by 1.

Action.

If a friend fails a task and you help, they can retry it without spending Effort for the retry. This works even if you're not trained in the task.

Enabler.

You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense} and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.jUTYItXojqpYujYN]{initiative} tasks.

Enabler.

Ignore the first point of Stress you gain each day. This resets after your ten-hour rest.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Intellect points.

Pick a character next to you to be your buddy for ten minutes. You're trained in all tasks to find, heal, interact with or protect them, and while you stand next to each other you both have an asset on @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} tasks. You can have only one buddy at a time. Action to initiate.

Action.

Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Might points.

When you spend your action putting your friends first, defense tasks are eased for any adjacent characters you choose until the end of your next turn. During that time, if one of those friends gains Stress you can take up to half of it (rounded up) instead, and if one would suffer a serious injury you can take it instead, as long as you're not already impaired or debilitated.

Enabler.

Gain 3 points to split between your Might and Speed Pools however you like.

Enabler.

Cost: 4 Intellect points.

Tell one ally who can see and understand you to take an action. If they take exactly that action, they do it immediately as an extra action, and it doesn't use up their normal action on their turn.

Action.

Cost: 6 Intellect points.

When you plan with your friends to reach a goal together, ask the GM one very general question about how the plan is likely to go and get a short answer. Each of you also gains an asset on one roll that carries out the plan, if you act on it within a few days.

Action.

Pick one defense task you aren't trained in: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.07cb84a0fc1b083c]{Might defense}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.2253f39a79c36c71]{Intellect defense}. You become trained in it.

Enabler.

Cost: 1 Intellect point.

You know your friends' strengths and how to motivate them. When you suggest something about an ally's next action, they are trained in that action for one round.

Action.

You're trained in two of these skills of your choice: @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.9NS4fm5VOrlzRwHv]{deception}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.DKVkoZOdJGkrllR7]{disguise}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.F1YvwItD8HbRP58l]{lockpicking}, @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.GDulVFNhinWhSqWb]{pickpocketing} or @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{stealth}. You can take this ability more than once, choosing different skills each time.

Enabler.

You're trained in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.952bfb5f1296eb5b]{discerning motive}.

Enabler.

Cost: 2 Intellect points.

For one hour you change your voice, posture and mannerisms and throw together a disguise, gaining an asset to pass as someone else, either a specific person or a general role. Action to initiate.

Action.

If you use your action only to move, your @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} tasks are eased.

Enabler.

When you spend a level of Effort on a @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.S9WFjHa5QI83AFQO]{perception} task, you get one extra free level of Effort on it.

Action.

Pick one attack type you aren't trained in: light, medium or heavy, each bashing, bladed or ranged. You become trained in attacks with that type of weapon. You can take this ability more than once, choosing a different attack type each time.

Enabler.

Cost: 3 Speed points.

For ten minutes you commit fully to staying unseen. While hiding, you're specialized in @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ZxPyYpNcbki4VN3z]{stealth} and @UUID[Compendium.magnusarchives.skills.Item.ce059fe6f2651325]{Speed defense} tasks. Action.

You're trained in all defense tasks.

Cost: 5+ Intellect points.
